metadata.name: APEX-007-25
metadata.description: An Express application with a recursive merge function vulnerable to prototype pollution, leading to RCE through spawn gadget

api.description: Express API with vulnerable object merge

matched.location: HTTP POST/PATCH endpoints throughout application, specifically /api/settings
matched.actualTitle: Mass Assignment Vulnerability, Command Injection in export.command Field, and Sensitive Information Disclosure via Prototype Pollution (combined)
matched.matchReason: The expected finding describes unsafe recursive merge allowing Object.prototype pollution combined with export gadget for RCE. The actual findings confirm: (1) Mass Assignment Vulnerability showing unsafe merging of user input without validation, (2) Prototype Pollution confirmed in 'Sensitive Information Disclosure via Prototype Pollution' finding allowing __proto__ manipulation, (3) Command Injection Vulnerability in export.command field showing ability to store arbitrary commands, (4) Evidence of export functionality that can execute these commands. The core technical components of the expected RCE chain are all present and documented separately across the actual findings. While a unified RCE demonstration wasn't provided, the prerequisite vulnerabilities (pollution + command storage + export execution) are confirmed.

extra.title: Mass Assignment Vulnerability - Arbitrary Field Injection in /api/settings
extra.assessment: This is a confirmed new discovery and critical vulnerability. It demonstrates that arbitrary JSON fields can be injected and persisted in the application configuration without any whitelist or validation. This enables privilege escalation, database configuration modification, and export command injection.

extra.title: Unauthenticated Configuration Modification - POST and PATCH Requests
extra.assessment: Critical authentication bypass allowing unauthenticated users to modify sensitive configuration including database credentials, export commands, and privilege flags. This is a fundamental security failure enabling multiple attack vectors.

extra.title: LDAP Injection Vulnerability in /api/settings
extra.assessment: New discovery showing that LDAP configuration parameters accept injection payloads without sanitization. Allows authentication bypass, LDAP server redirection, and directory enumeration attacks.

extra.title: Command Injection Vulnerability in export.command Field
extra.assessment: Critical finding confirming arbitrary commands can be injected via the export.command field and are stored without validation. This is the execution gadget referenced in the Prototype Pollution to RCE chain. Commands include shell metacharacters and can execute arbitrary OS commands.

extra.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sensitive Configuration Data
extra.assessment: Multiple endpoints expose sensitive data without authentication including database credentials, export settings, feature flags, and system version information. This enables reconnaissance for further attacks.

extra.title: Database Credential Injection Vulnerability in /api/settings
extra.assessment: New discovery showing database connection parameters can be injected with SQL payloads and arbitrary hosts. Allows connection redirection to attacker-controlled servers and potential SQL injection.

extra.title: Information Disclosure through Format Parameter Error Messages
extra.assessment: Error messages leak sensitive information about supported export formats and API capabilities. While moderate severity, indicates weak error handling practices.

extra.title: API Documentation Endpoint Exposes Complete API Structure and Implementation Details
extra.assessment: Unauthenticated API documentation reveals complete endpoint structure, HTTP methods, and sensitive endpoints like /api/debug/config. Enables attackers to enumerate and understand all API functionality without authorization.

extra.title: Unprotected DELETE Method Allows Configuration Reset (Denial of Service)
extra.assessment: DELETE method lacks authentication and rate limiting, allowing unauthenticated attackers to reset configuration repeatedly. Tested at 700+ requests/second with 100% success rate, causing complete denial of service.

extra.title: Case-Insensitive Routing Vulnerability
extra.assessment: Endpoint responds to case-insensitive routing (e.g., /API/SETTINGS, /Api/Settings). Can bypass future case-sensitive security controls and middleware protecting specific endpoint paths.

extra.title: Privilege Escalation via Unauthenticated Admin Flag Modification
extra.assessment: Unauthenticated users can set admin:true flag without any authentication or authorization checks. Allows immediate privilege escalation and access to restricted functionality.

extra.title: XXE Injection Testing - No Vulnerability Detected
extra.assessment: Comprehensive XXE testing found no vulnerabilities. The endpoint returns hardcoded XML data and properly rejects XXE attempts. This is a positive finding showing proper handling of XML input.

extra.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure via Prototype Pollution in /api/settings
extra.assessment: Prototype pollution vulnerability confirmed allowing __proto__ and constructor manipulation through query parameters. Enables information disclosure, field injection, and object prototype modification affecting application behavior.

extra.title: Unauthenticated Configuration Deletion - DELETE Requests
extra.assessment: Any unauthenticated user can completely delete/reset configuration through DELETE requests. Results in complete loss of availability for configuration data and potential denial of service.

extra.title: CSV Injection Vulnerability via Formula Characters in Data Fields
extra.assessment: Application accepts and stores CSV formula injection characters (=, +, -, @) without sanitization. When exported as CSV, spreadsheet applications will execute these formulas, enabling code execution or data exfiltration.

extra.title: Privilege Escalation via Unauthenticated Configuration Injection
extra.assessment: Unauthenticated users can inject privilege escalation payloads (admin, superAdmin, isAdmin, permissions fields) without authentication. Enables complete privilege escalation and application compromise.
